title: An elementary etale neighbourhood splits off finite pieces through given isolated fibre points of a separated morphism (Stacks 02LN)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $s\in S$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], with first projection $\iota:X_s\to X$ (a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(s)$). Let $n\ge0$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$ be pairwise distinct points with $f(x_i)=s$ such that each $x_i$ is an isolated point of $X_s$: the unique point $\xi_i\in X_s$ with $\iota(\xi_i)=x_i$ has $\{\xi_i\}$ open in $X_s$. Then there exist a scheme $U$, an etale morphism $\varphi:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ such that the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $\varphi$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism (an elementary etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$), and, writing $X_U=U\times_SX$ for the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:X_U\to X$ and $q:X_U\to U$, open subschemes $W,V_1,\dots,V_n$ of $X_U$ which are pairwise disjoint and cover $X_U$ (so each of them is also closed in $X_U$: $X_U=W\amalg V_1\amalg\cdots\amalg V_n$), such that: (i) for each $i$ the composite $V_i\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{q}U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; (ii) for each $i$ there is exactly one point $v_i\in V_i$ with $q(v_i)=u$; (iii) $p(v_i)=x_i$, and the map $\kappa(x_i)\to\kappa(v_i)$ induced by $p$ on residue fields is an isomorphism; (iv) no point $w\in W$ with $q(w)=u$ satisfies $p(w)\in\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$.

proof.text: The projection q from X times_S U to U is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. Each V_i to U is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Its inclusion into X times_S U is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. A proper map is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so its range V_i is closed (Scheme.Hom.isClosedMap.isClosed_range and Scheme.Opens.range_ι). No closed-immersion upgrade is necessary.

proof.text: The finite union of the retained closed opens V_i is closed (isClosed_iUnion_of_finite); construct W explicitly as its open complement. Pointwise membership proves Disjoint W V_i and W sup (iSup V_i) = top. This also handles n=0: the union is empty and W is the whole pullback.

proof.text: It remains to verify (iv), which is implicit in the final sentence of Stacks. Suppose $w\in W$ satisfies $q(w)=u$ and $p(w)=x_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], points of $X_U=X\times_SU$ mapping to $(x_i,u)$ correspond to primes of $\kappa(x_i)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u)$. Since the elementary neighbourhood gives an isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$, this tensor product is isomorphic to the field $\kappa(x_i)$ and has exactly one prime. Both $w$ and $v_i$ map to $(x_i,u)$, hence $w=v_i$. But $v_i\in V_i$ whereas $w\in W$, contradicting disjointness. Therefore no such $w$ exists. In Lean, reuse AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_point_unique from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePiecePersistence through a proof-only import all; this existing theorem proves the residue-field tensor-product uniqueness and is not duplicated locally. Finally use pullbackSymmetry and the preimageIso of each open to transport W and all V_i from X times_S U to U times_S X, preserving disjointness, the cover, finiteness, point uniqueness, residue-field maps, and avoidance.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement hypothesis by hypothesis against Stacks 02LN and kept it unchanged. Split its proof into five steps following 02LN: apply the elementary multi-point theorem 02LL; prove each finite open piece is closed using separated base change, finite implies proper, and proper over a separated target; remove the finitely many closed images of pairwise intersections and restrict all pieces; take the complementary open-and-closed W; and write out the source's implicit verification that W has no point over u mapping to any x_i using the fibre-product point description and kappa(s)=kappa(u). The n=0 case is explicit. No new nodes were needed; the item's existing LeanSearch, LeanFinder/Loogle, grep, and local-search records were checked and still show only Mathlib's weaker one-point theorem.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_splits_off_isolated_points {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f] (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (h_distinct : Function.Injective x) (h_over : ∀ i : Fin n, f (x i) = s) (h_isolated : ∀ i : Fin n, IsOpen ({f.asFiber (x i)} : Set (f.fiber (f (x i))))) : ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (φ : U ⟶ S) (t : U), Etale φ ∧ φ t = s ∧ IsIso (φ.residueFieldMap t) ∧ ∃ (W : (pullback φ f).Opens) (V : Fin n → (pullback φ f).Opens), (∀ i : Fin n, Disjoint W (V i)) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j)) ∧ W ⊔ (⨆ i : Fin n, V i) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, IsFinite ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst φ f)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, ∃ v : (V i).toScheme, ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst φ f) v = t ∧ (∀ v' : (V i).toScheme, ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst φ f) v' = t → v' = v) ∧ ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd φ f) v = x i ∧ IsIso (((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd φ f).residueFieldMap v)) ∧ (∀ w : W.toScheme, (W.ι ≫ pullback.fst φ f) w = t → ∀ i : Fin n, (W.ι ≫ pullback.snd φ f) w ≠ x i)
